title: Venus and the Moon strike a pose
caption: Venus, the crescent Moon and an Auxiliary Telescope at sunrise, Paranal Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The rising Sun fills the sky over Cerro Paranal in Chile with orange light. Above the dark outline of the mountains hang a crescent Moon and the bright planet Venus. In front stands the silhouette of an Auxiliary Telescope, part of ESO's Very Large Telescope.
The rest of the Moon's disc can also be seen, faintly lit. This is earthshine, sunlight reflected from the Earth onto the Moon and back to us again.

Babak Tafreshi on the left and Yuri Beletsky on the right, both on the ESO Fulldome Expedition, are setting up their tripods and cameras for the day. Their colleague, ESO Photo Ambassador Petr Horálek, caught the twilight moment. The expedition gathered images for the ESO Supernova Planetarium & Visitor Center, which at the time was being built at ESO's Headquarters in Garching, near Munich, Germany.

understand.summary: This is a sunrise landscape photograph by Petr Horálek. The source gives no camera or color details.
understand.eye: This is ordinary visible light, and earthshine can be seen by eye, though a camera can hold the bright crescent and its faint disc in one frame.
